question: Does lower error with nearby-family support reflect prediction of state-dependent variations, or mostly a family-average response?
sources: fixed15000 validation_center models,seeds42/43/44; existing original evaluation forecasts and their trained12neighbor support forecasts; no new training
definition: for every original pin-event query, collect the same-query12distinct signed/scale neighbor trajectories,ignoring repeated sampling slots. y=future100ms endpoints-current endpoints. Compute true neighbor mean and predicted neighbor mean. Held-center residual target=y_center-mean(y_neighbors); predicted residual=pred_y_center-mean(pred_y_neighbors).

metrics.held_center_residual_R2: 1-macro_episode_mean(mean_endpoint_squared_norm(predicted_residual-true_residual))/macro_episode_mean(mean_endpoint_squared_norm(true_residual)); zero corresponds to no prediction of deviation from the family mean
metrics.trained_neighbor_centered_R2: same centered variation score within the12training neighbors; average neighbor/endpoints then events/episode then episodes
metrics.privileged_family_mean_error: evaluation_current+true_neighbor_mean displacement compared with original evaluation truth; this baseline has explicit family/query association and must not be presented as a deployable nearest-neighbor method
metrics.uncertainty: 10000paired episode bootstrap with seed20261024 on the ratio,conditional on known families; average3seed numerator before resampling,also report everyseed

interpretation: Positive held-center R2 with95CI lower>0 supports prediction of family-centered variation; upper<=0 is evidence of failure to outperform a no-variation predictor for that component under this recipe. A crossing interval is inconclusive. This is secondary and never changes the original coverage decision,training budget or checkpoint.
limits: These families are intentionally exposed; no unseen-family generalization claim.
Support variation is scored on trained neighbors,so it can establish fit but not independent generalization.
A good family mean baseline can reflect simple regularity and does not prove information-theoretic input sufficiency.
